results.title: Arts & Sciences - Answers Knowledge Base
results.content: Students may register for an additional practicum course (M.F.T. 764) should they need additional time to complete the clinical requirements of the program. Residential students typically begin to see clients in the Couple and Family Therapy Center at the beginning of the second semester in the M.F.T. core unless the faculty decide on the basis of performance in the Fall courses that they are not clinically ready to do so. The policy of A.A.M.F.T. is that the M.A. degree is the qualifying degree for the field and, therefore, a person should not hold themselves out as a marriage and family student therapist before having received a M.A. in Marriage and Family Therapy or having completed an equivalent program of study. All M.F.T. doctoral students are expected to continue clinical practice throughout their graduate study and to complete, prior to graduation, the 1000 supervised client contact hours with individuals, couples, and families.
